title: Spotted Dick
subtitle: British steamed suet pudding with currants and custard
excerpt: Spotted dick is one of the great British steamed puddings: a suet sponge studded with currants, served warm with custard or clotted cream. The name refers to the currants (the spots) and the old word dick which may derive from dough or pudding. It is old-fashioned, unapologetically stodgy, and completely wonderful on a cold evening.
sourceNotes: Spotted dick is a traditional British steamed pudding that has been made since at least the mid-19th century. It appears in Mrs Beeton's Book of Household Management (1861). The pudding is part of the broader tradition of British suet puddings -- a family that includes treacle sponge, jam roly-poly, and steak and kidney pudding. All use suet as their fat and are steamed rather than baked.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze after steaming. Reheat by steaming for 30 minutes from frozen.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made up to 2 days ahead. Reheat by steaming for 20 minutes.

content.text: Spotted dick is traditionally steamed in a roll of greaseproof paper, shaped like a log, rather than in a basin. This gives it an attractive round cross-section when sliced. It can also be steamed in a pudding basin if preferred. The pudding steams for 1.5 hours -- the water must be topped up regularly.

Mix {{plain-flour}} flour, {{suet-shredded}} suet, {{caster-sugar}} caster sugar, {{baking-powder}} baking powder, {{currants}} currants, {{lemon}} lemon zest, and {{salt-table}} salt in a bowl. Add {{whole-milk}} milk a little at a time. Stop when the dough is soft but not sticky.

Turn the dough onto a large sheet of greaseproof paper and shape into a log about 20 cm long. Roll the paper around the log and twist the ends tightly. Place in a steamer basket over a pan of simmering water, or lay across the top of a pan with the ends resting on the rim. Steam for 1.5 hours, topping up the water every 30 minutes.
Remove the paper carefully -- the pudding will be very hot and steamy. Slice and serve with hot custard or clotted cream.

items.symptom: The pudding is dense and heavy
items.cause: Too much milk was added, the mixture was overworked, or the baking powder was old.
items.fix: Suet pudding should be just brought together without kneading. Use fresh baking powder. The pudding will always be denser than a baked sponge -- that is its nature -- but it should not be solid. A properly made spotted dick is moist and slightly yielding, not brick-like.

content.text: Spotted dick is one of the best-known and most joked-about dishes in British cooking. It is a staple of school dinners, hospital canteens, and traditional British restaurants. The dish has been on the menu of the Houses of Parliament in London for many decades and is considered part of British cultural heritage. Despite its old-fashioned associations, it remains widely eaten and widely loved.
